description: Return the ratios FinancialMD computes from a company's standardized facts: gross, operating, net and free cash flow margins, revenue growth year over year, return on equity and on assets, asset turnover, current ratio, debt to equity, interest coverage, basic and diluted EPS; for banks net interest income to average loans and securities (not the bank's reported NIM), efficiency ratio and loans to deposits; for insurers loss and acquisition cost ratios; and valuation at each period end (market cap, EV, P/E, P/S, P/B, EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT, FCF and dividend yield) from the last IEX close on or before the period end (data.price_basis says which close, or why valuation is empty: several share classes, an ADR, no prices). The result has the statement grid shape (periods most recent first, one row per ratio, cells aligned with periods); margins and growth are fractions (0.462 is 46.2 percent). Every cell is a value object whose proof lists the proof ids of its inputs (proof.inputs) and whose method is derived_lineitem; proof_get on a ratio proof returns the inputs and the formula. A cell is null when an input is missing (a bank has no gross margin) or a denominator is zero: never NaN. as_of computes from the facts known on that date. For valuation on every trading day use ratios_daily. Use it when the question is about margins, returns, leverage, growth or valuation at period ends.

as_of.description: Knowledge date or timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339). The answer is what FinancialMD knew at that instant: only facts whose known interval contains as_of. Omit for the current view.

company.description: Company identifier: a FinancialMD id ("fmd_01H..."), an SEC CIK ("cik:320193"), or a ticker ("ticker:AAPL", optionally with the MIC "ticker:AAPL.XNAS"). A bare ticker like "AAPL" is accepted and sent as ticker:AAPL. An issuer on an EU or UK regulated market that does not file with the SEC has no CIK: pass its LEI ("lei:IOG4E947OATN0KJYSD45") or its fmd_ id.

limit.description: Maximum number of periods or items to return (default 10, at most 200).

period_type.description: Period basis: annual (fiscal years), quarterly, ltm (last twelve months) or ytd (year to date).

ratios.description: Optional: only these ratio ids (the grid is trimmed client-side; the call costs the same).

name: ratios

outputSchema.description: The FinancialMD envelope (docs/API.md section 2): data plus meta (request_id, as_of knowledge time, matched company, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base). Every numeric value inside data is an object with value, unit, currency, period, known interval, restated flag, method and a proof pointing at the filing. On failure the result is isError with an error object instead.

data.description: The ratio grid: statement "ratios", period_type, view, currency, periods (most recent first) and one row per ratio id with cells aligned to periods.

anyOf.description: A proven number: value, unit, currency, decimals, period, known interval, restated, method, calc_type, proof.

proof.description: Where a value comes from: filing accession, form, filing date, taxonomy and tag, source URL, page and anchor.

inputs.description: For derived values (ratios): the proof ids of the inputs.

items.description: A proven number: value, unit, currency, decimals, period, known interval, restated, method, calc_type, proof.

proof.description: Where a value comes from: filing accession, form, filing date, taxonomy and tag, source URL, page and anchor.

inputs.description: For derived values (ratios): the proof ids of the inputs.

items.description: A value object, null when the concept has no value for the period, or { versions: [...] } oldest first with history=true.

fiscal_alias.description: Deprecated twin of metric_alias, served for one more release.

error.description: Present only on isError results: the API error code and message plus remedy hints.

meta.description: Request metadata: request_id, as_of, company resolution, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base.

attribution.description: Citations a source requires on anything shown from the answer.
